name: @projexlight/sdk-lead-scoring
summary: Per-tenant lead-scoring engine: declarative weighted-feature models + on-demand or event-driven score recomputation. Scores publish to sdk-crm.lead/contact + push out to Salesforce/HubSpot via connector exports. Compliant by design — every score is traceable to the contributing features for any regulator who asks 'why was this lead prioritized'.

endpoints.description: Fetch a model definition + active version + feature weights.
Activate a new model version; scoring switches over atomically.
Retire a model version; historic scores remain readable.
Score a cohort of leads (async; returns a job_id).
Fetch the current score + contributing features for one lead.
All historical scores for one lead (audit / drift analysis).
Update feature weights for the active model version (creates a new draft version).

events.name: lead_scoring.model.published.v1
events.description: New model version published; carries feature weights + activation timestamp.

events.name: lead_scoring.score.computed.v1
events.description: Lead scored; carries score, contributing features + their weights, model version.

events.name: lead_scoring.score.changed.v1
events.description: Score crossed a configured threshold; triggers downstream workflows.

models.description: Per-model row: name, version, status (draft/active/retired), defined_at.
Per-(lead, model_version) row: score, contributing_features_json, computed_at.
Per-(model_version, feature) row: weight, source, last_updated_at.

hooks.name: publishModelVersion
hooks.description: Draft → publish a new model version + activate it atomically.

hooks.name: scoreLead
hooks.description: Score one lead; idempotent on (lead_id, model_version).

hooks.name: scoreBulk
hooks.description: Async batch scoring; returns a job_id.

hooks.name: explainScore
hooks.description: Return the score + contributing features + weights for one lead (regulator / SDR view).

hooks.name: startDriftMonitor
hooks.description: Background worker: flags weight-drift between draft + active model.

scenarios.title: Publish v2 of the MQL scoring model with new firmographic weights
scenarios.when_to_use: Analytics team validated new weights against historical conversions; publish as v2 + activate.
scenarios.expected_outcome: v2 active for new scores; v1 still readable for historic. Emits .model.published.v1.

scenarios.title: Re-score lead after a demo encounter completes
scenarios.when_to_use: Reactive on engagement.encounter.completed.v1 with kind='demo' — demo attendance is a strong signal, re-score immediately so SDRs route hot leads to AEs.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Score recomputed; emits .score.computed.v1 + .score.changed.v1 if crossed threshold.

scenarios.title: Bulk re-score every active lead after model v2
scenarios.when_to_use: v2 activated; we want the AE board to reflect the new ordering by tomorrow morning. Bulk job runs overnight.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Job_id returned. Per-batch progress visible via job status endpoint. Each lead emits .score.computed.v1.

scenarios.title: Regulator asks: 'why was this contact prioritized?'
scenarios.when_to_use: GDPR Art-22 / EU AI Act request — the explanation API returns the score + every contributing feature + its weight at the time of scoring.
scenarios.expected_outcome: Full reproducible scoring trace returned. Sufficient for regulator + internal SDR coaching.

scenarios.title: Drift monitor flags weight divergence between draft + active
scenarios.when_to_use: Data scientist edits the draft (mql-v3); drift monitor periodically checks if the draft's predicted score distribution diverges materially from active. If yes, alerts the data team.
scenarios.example_code:
import { startDriftMonitor } from '@projexlight/sdk-lead-scoring';
startDriftMonitor({ tenant_id, model_id: 'mql', interval_hours: 24 });
scenarios.expected_outcome: Daily KS-test on score distributions; if divergence > threshold, alert posted via sdk-notification.

compliance_posture.notes: Every score is fully reproducible — model version pinned + contributing features snapshotted. EU AI Act decision-trace requirement met for downstream automated routing. Weights audited on publish so a model can't change retroactively.
